design_detail: Registry homepage (MGH National Pregnancy Registry for Psychiatric Medications); web resource
population: Registry of pregnant women exposed to psychiatric medications (website)
sample_size_detail: Website; no study data in file
rationale: Citation is to a registry web page accessed online; file has no abstract or study content. Coded as a resource, not a study.

design_detail: AHRQ Comparative Effectiveness Review No. 236; systematic review of perinatal pharmacologic interventions
comparison_group: Placebo, no treatment, other pharmacotherapy, or discontinuation before pregnancy
population: Pregnant, postpartum, or reproductive-age women with mental health disorders treated with pharmacotherapy
sample_size_detail: 164 studies (168 articles); pooled participant total not reported (outcome-specific Ns such as 209, 36, 2608 given)
rationale: AHRQ systematic review searching four databases through June 2020. Includes RCTs (brexanolone, sertraline) and observational studies; 'More than 95 percent of studies reporting on harms were observational'.

design_detail: Population-based register cohort, linked prenatal SSRI prescriptions and birth records (1998–2001), propensity-score matching
severity_measure: Abstract says PS matching controlled 'maternal illness severity' via maternal health characteristics and total exposure; specific variables not listed
comparison_group: SSRI-exposed neonates whose exposure stopped before the last 14 days of gestation (NL14)
population: Neonates with prenatal SSRI exposure in linked population health data, 1998–2001
sample_size_detail: 119547 linked neonatal birth records = source population; numbers of L14 vs NL14 SSRI-exposed neonates in the matched analysis not given in abstract
rationale: Exposure-timing comparison (last-14-day vs earlier SSRI exposure) with propensity score matching. Conclusion states results are 'controlling for maternal illness severity', but the covariate list is not shown; analytic N not reported.

design_detail: Retrospective hospital cohort (2007–2012) of antidepressant-exposed infants; risk-factor analysis for poor neonatal adaptation (Finnegan score)
severity_measure: Risk factors analysed included maternal anxiety and depression (apparently presence, not severity); abstract does not state whether ORs were multivariable-adjusted
comparison_group: Within exposed infants: SNRI vs SSRI exposure; breast/mixed vs formula feeding; dose levels
population: Infants exposed to antidepressants in the last trimester, maternity ward of a general hospital, 2007–2012
sample_size_detail: 247 infants included; 157 (64%) developed PNA
rationale: Non-randomized risk-factor comparison within exposed infants reporting ORs. Abstract does not describe multivariable adjustment, so coded unadjusted with severity Unclear.

design_detail: NICE clinical guideline CG192 (antenatal and postnatal mental health)
population: Women planning pregnancy, pregnant, or up to 1 year postpartum with mental health problems (UK guideline)
sample_size_detail: Guideline; no sample
rationale: PubMed type 'Practice Guideline'; NICE clinical guideline covering recognition, assessment and treatment of perinatal mental health problems.

design_detail: RNAO best practice guideline (assessment and interventions for perinatal depression)
population: Perinatal depression (nursing best practice guideline, Ontario)
sample_size_detail: Guideline; no sample
rationale: Citation describes a 'Best practice guideline' from the Registered Nurses' Association of Ontario; no abstract or study content in file.

design_detail: Cross-sectional mailed survey (36 questions) of obstetrician-gynecologists
severity_measure: Survey of clinicians; not a treatment comparison
population: Obstetrician-gynecologists (US), depression screening attitudes and practices
sample_size_detail: 282 ob-gyns completed the survey; response rate not given in abstract
rationale: Clinician survey of depression screening attitudes and practices; predictors of screening reported but design is a survey.

design_detail: Web page for Postpartum Support International frontline provider trainings
population: Training program for providers in perinatal mental health (website)
sample_size_detail: Website; no study data
rationale: Citation is to an online training-program page; training programs are coded as resources.

design_detail: Multiple-treatments (network) meta-analysis of RCTs of 12 new-generation antidepressants for acute unipolar major depression
population: Adults with unipolar major depression in RCTs, 1991–Nov 2007
sample_size_detail: 117 RCTs with 25928 participants
rationale: Systematic review and network meta-analysis restricted to 117 randomised controlled trials; ITT analysis.

design_detail: Population-based descriptive case series of pregnancy-associated deaths from self-harm (overdose or suicide), Colorado 2004–2012, record abstraction
severity_measure: Purely descriptive; no comparative effect estimate
comparison_group: None (descriptive context vs all Colorado live births, no statistical comparison)
population: Women with pregnancy-associated deaths from self-harm in Colorado, 2004–2012
sample_size_detail: 211 maternal deaths; 63 from self-harm (used for mortality ratios); detailed records for 59 (31 overdose, 28 suicide) analysed; context 614154 live births
rationale: Authors call it a case series with 'Descriptive analyses were performed'; it computes statewide mortality ratios from surveillance data, so coded descriptive observational (first fitting code) rather than case series.

design_detail: Prospective clinical cohort at a perinatal psychiatry service; factors associated with SSRI discontinuation upon pregnancy confirmation
severity_measure: EPDS and STAI were measured and compared between groups; abstract does not describe covariate adjustment for the OR
comparison_group: Women who maintained SSRI treatment (vs discontinued)
population: Pregnant women with DSM-IV depressive or anxiety disorder on SSRIs at conception, Hospital Clínic Barcelona, 2005–2008
sample_size_detail: 132 women; 70 discontinued, 62 maintained; 40 of 70 reintroduced
rationale: Observational comparison of discontinuers vs maintainers; bivariate comparisons and a single OR for unplanned pregnancy reported with no adjustment described.

design_detail: Prospective naturalistic multicenter cohort with monthly psychiatric assessments; survival analysis of time to relapse
severity_measure: Abstract does not state whether the hazard ratio was adjusted or for what; sample restricted to MDD history and euthymia (diagnosis-based restriction)
comparison_group: Women who maintained antidepressant medication throughout pregnancy
population: Pregnant women with history of major depression, euthymic on antidepressants near conception, 3 specialty centers, 1999–2003
sample_size_detail: 201 enrolled; 82 maintained vs 65 discontinued in the main contrast; 13 miscarried, 5 terminated, 12 lost, 8 withdrew
rationale: Non-randomized comparison of discontinuation vs maintenance; HR 5.0 from survival analysis but no covariates described in the abstract, so coded unadjusted with severity Unclear.

design_detail: Program utilization and quality assessment of MCPAP for Moms (encounter data 2014–2017) plus focus groups and in-depth interviews (grounded theory)
severity_measure: Program evaluation; no comparative effect estimate
population: Pregnant/postpartum women served and obstetric providers/practices using MCPAP for Moms, Massachusetts, June 2014–Dec 2017
sample_size_detail: 3699 women served; 145 practices enrolled; 1174 providers trained; 7444 encounters; 3 provider focus groups (36 participants) and 10 patient interviews
rationale: Describes program utilization (counts, percentages) and qualitative themes; no comparison group or effect estimate.

design_detail: Updated systematic review and meta-analysis/mixed-treatment comparisons of second-generation antidepressants for MDD (AHRQ-funded)
population: Adults with major depressive disorder, studies 1980–Aug 2011
sample_size_detail: 234 studies; RCTs (>=6 weeks) for efficacy and observational studies (>=1000 participants) for harms; pooled N not reported in abstract
rationale: Systematic review with meta-analyses; included randomized trials for efficacy and large observational studies for harms.

design_detail: FDA Drug Safety Communication on SSRI use in pregnancy and PPHN (regulatory notice)
population: Pregnant women using SSRIs and their newborns (regulatory communication)
sample_size_detail: Regulatory notice; no sample
rationale: Citation is an FDA drug safety communication web page, i.e., a regulatory notice.

design_detail: Retrospective cohort nested in US Medicaid Analytic eXtract 2000–2010; restricted to depression diagnosis; logistic regression with PS and high-dimensional PS stratification
severity_measure: Number of outpatient and inpatient depression diagnoses (labelled 'proxies for depression severity'); also other psychotropic drugs and health care use
comparison_group: Women with depression diagnosis unexposed to antidepressants during pregnancy
population: Pregnant women enrolled in US Medicaid (46 states + DC), 2000–2010, with linked live-born infants
sample_size_detail: Depression-restricted cohort used for primary adjusted estimates: 657515 unexposed, 65316 SSRI, 16283 non-SSRI; full eligible cohort 3789330 pregnancies (102179 SSRI, 26771 non-SSRI)
rationale: PS model included 'proxies for depression severity (number of outpatient and inpatient depression diagnoses)' within a depression-restricted cohort. N reported for the depression-restricted analytic cohort rather than the 3789330 source cohort.

design_detail: Two-site, 3-arm placebo-controlled RCT, 12 weeks: IPT vs sertraline + clinical management vs pill placebo + clinical management
comparison_group: Pill placebo with clinical management (and IPT arm)
population: Breastfeeding and non-breastfeeding women with a major depressive episode in the first postpartum year, Iowa and Rhode Island
sample_size_detail: 162 randomized; number analyzed not reported in abstract
rationale: Women 'were randomly assigned to IPT, sertraline-clinical management (CM), or pill placebo-CM'.

design_detail: Meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials of brexanolone infusion for postpartum depression
population: Women with postpartum depression in brexanolone RCTs
sample_size_detail: 2 articles reporting 3 RCTs (4 active arms); 156 brexanolone, 111 placebo
rationale: Only RCTs were included; pooled n = 267 women with PPD.

design_detail: FDA-approved REMS program page for Zulresso (brexanolone) (regulatory resource)
population: Patients receiving brexanolone for postpartum depression (regulatory program)
sample_size_detail: Regulatory resource; no sample
rationale: Citation is an FDA REMS web page, coded as a regulatory resource.

design_detail: Meta-analysis of RCTs of evidence-based psychotherapies and medications for GAD vs control conditions (random effects, Hedges g, meta-regression)
comparison_group: Waitlist, TAU, pill placebo, or psychological placebo
population: Adults with DSM-diagnosed generalized anxiety disorder (children excluded), studies through June 2017
sample_size_detail: 79 RCTs with 11002 participants
rationale: Systematic search with RCT-only inclusion; 'Sixty-one were not RCT' and were excluded.

design_detail: Clinical overview of diagnosis and management of perinatal anxiety in the obstetric setting
population: Women with perinatal anxiety (clinical review)
sample_size_detail: Narrative review; no sample
rationale: Authors provide a summary 'Informed by our clinical practice'; no systematic methods described.

design_detail: Meta-analytic review of randomized placebo-controlled trials of SSRIs, SNRIs, and benzodiazepines for adult GAD (random effects, meta-regression)
population: Adults with primary DSM diagnosis of GAD in placebo-controlled trials
sample_size_detail: 54 articles reporting 56 unique trials; 12655 participants (6464 active drug, 6191 placebo)
rationale: Inclusion required a randomized, placebo-controlled trial; 56 trials pooled.

design_detail: Meta-analysis of cohort and case-control studies of first-trimester benzodiazepine exposure and major malformations/oral cleft (random effects)
comparison_group: Unexposed pregnancies (cohort) / non-cases (case-control) in included studies
population: Pregnancies with first-trimester benzodiazepine exposure, studies 1966 onward
sample_size_detail: 23 studies included (cohort and case-control analysed separately); pooled N not reported
rationale: Meta-analysis of 'concurrently controlled' cohort and case-control studies.

design_detail: Systematic review and meta-analysis (PRISMA/MOOSE) of longitudinal studies of recurrence after first-onset postpartum psychosis
population: Women with first-onset postpartum psychosis followed >=18 months
sample_size_detail: 6 studies, 645 patients; follow-up 11–26 years
rationale: Random-effects pooled recurrence estimate from six longitudinal observational studies.

design_detail: Population-based record-linkage cohort (psychiatric case register + obstetric data), Western Australia 1980–1992, vs random comparison sample
severity_measure: Abstract says only that odds ratios were calculated; no covariates described. Exposure is maternal illness, not treatment
comparison_group: Births to women without a psychiatric diagnosis (randomly selected)
population: Births to women with schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, or major depression in Western Australia, 1980–1992
sample_size_detail: 3174 births to women with schizophrenia/major affective disorders; 3129 comparison births
rationale: Compares complications in births to mentally ill vs comparison women using ORs; no adjustment described. Abstract also compares pregnancies before vs after diagnosis, possibly within women, so sibling/within-mother coded Unclear.

design_detail: Prospective observational population pharmacokinetic study; nonlinear mixed-effects (NONMEM) model of lamotrigine oral clearance across pregnancy and postpartum
severity_measure: PK study; no confounder-adjusted clinical outcome comparison
population: Women with epilepsy and/or psychiatric disorder (mostly bipolar) on lamotrigine who were pregnant or planning pregnancy, Emory
sample_size_detail: 60 women (64 pregnancies), 600 lamotrigine concentrations
rationale: Models lamotrigine clearance by gestational week and postpartum weeks; purely pharmacokinetic.

design_detail: Retrospective population-based prevalence/trend study in 11 US health plans (MEPREP), 2001–2007; descriptive prevalence of prenatal antipsychotic use
severity_measure: Purely descriptive prevalence; no effect estimate
comparison_group: None (descriptive comparison of characteristics with unexposed deliveries)
population: Live-born deliveries to women aged 15–45 in 11 US health plans, 2001–2007
sample_size_detail: 585615 deliveries; 4223 atypical and 548 typical antipsychotic-exposed
rationale: Estimates prevalence and temporal trends of antipsychotic use by year, trimester, and diagnosis; descriptive only.

design_detail: Prospective pregnancy registry cohort (MGH National Pregnancy Registry for Atypical Antipsychotics) with medical record confirmation
severity_measure: Abstract never states whether the OR is adjusted (Amendment 1b); the OR 1.25 matches crude counts (3/214 vs 1/89)
comparison_group: Unexposed infants of mothers with histories of psychiatric morbidity
population: Pregnant women aged 18–45 enrolled in a US national registry through Dec 2014
sample_size_detail: 487 enrolled (353 SGA users, 134 comparison); 303 eligible for analysis: 214 first-trimester-exposed live births vs 89 controls
rationale: Registry cohort reporting an OR with no statement on adjustment, so Amendment 1(b) applies. The OR and absolute risks (1.4% vs 1.1%) are consistent with a crude comparison.

design_detail: Prospective observational cohort (Pittsburgh, 2006–2011); repeated-measures mixed models of BSID-II scores, unadjusted (Model I) then adjusted for symptom scores and confounders (Models II–III)
severity_measure: Maternal SIGH-ADS (Hamilton depression with atypical supplement) and Mania Rating Scale scores entered Models II and III
comparison_group: Infants of women with untreated bipolar disorder (BD−) and infants unexposed to bipolar disorder or psychotropics
population: Mother-infant dyads with maternal bipolar disorder treated or untreated with psychotropics in pregnancy, plus unexposed controls
sample_size_detail: 197 dyads: 54 BD+, 27 BD−, 116 nonexposed; attrition over 52 weeks
rationale: Model II 'added SIGH-ADS and MRS scores' to control for symptomatology. Note that the abstract's headline P values come from the unadjusted Model I.

design_detail: Descriptive surveillance report (MMWR) of spina bifida incidence from 16 state population-based birth defects surveillance systems, 1983–1990
population: Births in 16 US states with population-based birth defects surveillance, 1983–1990
sample_size_detail: Number of births/cases not given in truncated abstract
rationale: CDC analysis 'to determine the incidence and descriptive epidemiology of spina bifida'; abstract truncated, no N available.

design_detail: Retrospective multicenter cohort of children of mothers with epilepsy using AEDs in first trimester vs matched nonepileptic controls, Netherlands 1972–1992
severity_measure: Controls described as 'matched' but matching factors and any other adjustment not listed; no seizure type/frequency mentioned
comparison_group: Nonepileptic matched control children (and comparisons across AED regimens)
population: Children born 1972–1992 in four Dutch provinces to mothers with epilepsy using AEDs in first trimester
sample_size_detail: 1411 AED-exposed children + 2000 nonepileptic matched controls
rationale: Relative risks by AED regimen against matched controls; matching counts as adjustment but covariates unstated, so severity Unclear.

design_detail: Prospective single-center cohort of pregnancies in women with epilepsy (San Paolo Hospital, Milan, since 1977) with standardized infant examination
severity_measure: Malformation rates reported descriptively; crude treated vs untreated comparison only
population: Pregnancies of women with epilepsy followed in Milan from 1977
sample_size_detail: 517 pregnancies followed; 25 untreated patients
rationale: Reports overall malformation rate (9.7%) by category and notes no malformations among 25 untreated patients; no adjustment described.

design_detail: Narrative review of animal and human data on anticonvulsant teratogenicity
population: Pregnant women exposed to anticonvulsants and experimental animals
sample_size_detail: Narrative review; no sample
rationale: Abstract summarizes animal and human literature and gives clinical advice; no original data or systematic methods.

design_detail: Case-control study within the Spanish Collaborative Study of Congenital Malformations (ECEMC) registry; OR controlled for potential confounders
severity_measure: OR 'after controlling for potential confounder factors' but factors not listed; no epilepsy severity mentioned
population: Malformed and control newborn infants in the Spanish ECEMC surveillance program
sample_size_detail: 22294 malformed infants + 21937 controls with AED data; 57 cases and 10 controls VPA-exposed; limb-deficiency case count for the OR not given
rationale: Case-control design with confounder-adjusted OR (6.17) for limb deficiencies; covariate list unavailable.

design_detail: Letter to the editor (J Pediatr 1983) on possible teratogenic effect of valproate; content not available
severity_measure: Presumed case description; no comparison evident
population: Infants exposed prenatally to valproate (presumed from title)
sample_size_detail: No abstract in file; number of cases unknown
rationale: File has metadata only (PubMed type 'Letter', no abstract). The title suggests a report of observed exposed cases, but the design cannot be verified.

design_detail: Case report of two VPA-exposed siblings with long-term follow-up plus a non-systematic literature compilation of VPA-monotherapy cases (1978–2000)
population: Children with prenatal valproic acid monotherapy exposure (fetal valproate syndrome)
sample_size_detail: 2 new sibling cases described; literature review identified 69 VPA-only exposed cases, which are the basis for the reported percentages
rationale: Describes exposed cases without a comparison group. N set to the 69-case compilation that underlies the summary statistics; the paper's own new cases number 2.

design_detail: Clinical case series of children with fetal anticonvulsant syndromes, ascertained via a support association and a genetics service; questionnaire, interview, examination
population: Children with fetal anticonvulsant syndromes (UK ascertainment via association and Aberdeen genetics service)
sample_size_detail: 57 children (52 via association, 5 referred); 34 valproate-only
rationale: Describes the phenotype of 57 exposed affected children with no unexposed comparison.

design_detail: Unselected case series of valproate-exposed infants of epileptic mothers, with within-series dose associations
population: Infants born to epileptic mothers exposed to sodium valproate in pregnancy
sample_size_detail: 17 exposed infants
rationale: Describes malformations and withdrawal in 17 exposed infants; dose associations are within the exposed series only.

design_detail: AIUM practice parameter for performance of fetal echocardiography
population: Pregnancies undergoing fetal echocardiography
sample_size_detail: Practice parameter; no sample
rationale: PubMed type 'Practice Guideline'; titled 'Practice Parameter'. No abstract in file.

design_detail: Prospective placental-passage study (maternal and cord lithium levels at delivery) pooled with literature cases; crude correlations with perinatal outcomes
severity_measure: PK/placental passage; outcome associations by lithium concentration without confounder adjustment
comparison_group: Infants with lower vs higher lithium concentrations at delivery (within exposed)
population: Pregnant women treated with lithium through delivery and their infants
sample_size_detail: 10 prospectively studied participants + 32 published cases pooled
rationale: Primary aim is quantifying lithium placental passage (cord:maternal ratio); outcome associations are crude comparisons by concentration.

design_detail: Retrospective cohort in US Medicaid Analytic eXtract 2000–2007, restricted to mood/anxiety disorder diagnoses; GEE regression adjusted for confounders plus high-dimensional PS sensitivity
severity_measure: Number of outpatient (0,1,2–5,6–9,>=10) and inpatient (0,1,>=2) mood/anxiety disorder diagnoses, labelled 'proxies of mood/anxiety disorder severity'
comparison_group: Women with mood/anxiety disorder unexposed to antidepressants in the 5 months before delivery
population: Pregnant women aged 12–55 in US Medicaid with mood or anxiety disorder diagnoses, deliveries 2000–2007
sample_size_detail: 106000 mood/anxiety subcohort minus 3278 polytherapy = 102722 analysed (69044 unexposed; 29222 SRI monotherapy, 12710 current; 4456 non-SRI monotherapy, 1495 current); source 2759414 pregnancies
rationale: Models adjusted for 'indicators of severity of mood/anxiety disorder' (numbers of outpatient/inpatient diagnoses) within a diagnosis-restricted cohort; robust variances for repeat pregnancies, no sibling contrast.

design_detail: Prospective national register-based birth cohort, Finland 1996–2010; SSRI-exposed vs unmedicated (depression-related diagnosis) vs unexposed offspring; hazard ratios
severity_measure: Comparison restricted to mothers with depression-related diagnoses (diagnosis only); abstract does not describe covariate adjustment
comparison_group: Offspring of mothers with depression-related psychiatric disorders without SSRI purchases (unmedicated); also unexposed offspring
population: Singleton offspring in Finnish national registers, 1996–2010, followed to age 14
sample_size_detail: 56340 offspring in final cohort: 15596 SSRI-exposed, 9537 unmedicated, 31207 unexposed; sampling frame 845345 pregnant women
rationale: Main contrast is SSRI-exposed vs unmedicated offspring of mothers with depression-related diagnoses. HRs are reported, but the abstract gives no adjustment or covariates, so coded unadjusted with severity Unclear.
